items.title: The Million Dollar Homepage, but for AI Agents
items.raw_excerpt: The Million Dollar Homepage (2005) let anyone buy pixels on a webpage via Paypal plus emailing your image to the site owner. Million Dollar Bot Page is the same idea, except every purchase and placement is made by an AI agent. Payments use MPP (Machine Payment Protocol) by Tempo x Stripe. The API returns a 402 with a WWW-Authenticate header, the agent's MPP client negotiates payment automatically, and retries the request. The agent can also generate images for you and our server validates before accepting. Whole thing works without a human in the loop.

items.title: 从卖寝具到提供睡眠系统服务：慕思的“用户终身价值”棋局
items.raw_excerpt: 当“睡个好觉”成为当代人普遍的奢侈品，睡眠经济便毫无悬念地站上了风口。 从褪黑素到助眠APP，从智能手环到睡眠喷雾，无数创业公司和资本竞相涌入，试图在这个千亿级市场中分一杯羹。 然而，喧嚣背后，一个核心问题始终悬而未决：这些零散的单点解决方案，真的能解决系统性睡眠问题吗？用户需要的究竟是更多数据，还是一个能真正理解并守护睡眠的“伙伴”？ 3月20日，世界睡眠日的前一天，一场由慕思携手华为鸿蒙举办，在麻省理工学院学术带头人、中国睡眠协会会长等嘉宾见证下的新品发布会，尝试给出了一个不一样的答案。 在这场以“鸿蒙智选慕思智能床Pro H-Design”为核心的发布会上，我们看到的不仅是一款新品的亮相，更是一个关于“睡眠3.0时代”的完整构想——当深耕睡眠研究的硬件与追求万物互联的生态深度融合，一张“懂你的床”正成为撬动全屋智能、开启全生命周期健康管理的关键支点。 当硬件陷入“堆料”迷思，睡眠系统服务才是终局 智能睡眠赛道正经历着前所未有的资本狂欢。 2026年开年，小米前高管范典创立的AI睡眠灯品牌Sleepal，首款产品在CES上斩获3项创新奖，即将开启海外众筹。 几乎同一时间，美国脑健康科技公司NextSense完成1600万美元A轮融资，推出全球首款内置临床级脑电传感器的真无线AI耳机，通过耳道电极采集脑电信号，可精准识别睡眠分期并强化深睡。 前不久，空间 Agentic AI 公司 Fullive.AI，成立一个月内连续完成种子轮及种子+轮融资，高瓴创投、智元机器人等机构联合押注，正致力于研发首款睡眠空间AI硬件，试图用“空间Agent”重构AI健康硬件生态。资本正用真金白银为睡眠科技赛道投下了信任票。 这股热潮并非凭空而起。 据市场研究机构数据显示，全球睡眠技术设备市场规模预计将从2025年的252.6亿美元增长到2026年的296.2亿美元，年复合增长率达17.2%。

excerpt_i18n.en:
Refrigerator magnets and commemorative coins, printed and dried instantly, with the next customer ready in two minutes. On March 17, 2026, at Hall 8.1 of the National Exhibition and Convention Center, a crowd lined up in front of a device. This was not a flagship product from an international brand, but the Mojo 1—a desktop consumer-grade UV printer on the Atomic Remodeling booth. Not far away, the 12 nozzles of the Palette 300 were operating simultaneously, forming a complex model in one go.  

But the buzz wasn’t limited to just one booth. Flashforge, Wande Mei, Xianyi… just a short distance from the Atomic Remodeling booth, multi-head 3D printers debuted in clusters, with several also showcasing their full-color 3D printers. No one was content to play a supporting role.  

"Multi-head" versus "full-color"—two technological paths clashed head-on in the same aisle. It wasn’t about one replacing the other; both were vying for the same goal: to become the protagonist in the next wave of desktop manufacturing.  

Behind this hardware race, another "hidden storyline" was emerging: AI 3D modeling software companies like Tripo AI and Hitem3D AI, with their extremely low creative barriers, quietly bridged the critical gap from "idea" to "physical object."  

Leiphone’s Hard Innovation Alliance, along with senior investors from two dollar funds and two RMB funds, and a 3D printer industry review blogger, teamed up to explore the 2026 TCT Asia exhibition, seeking an answer: as multi-head 3D printing, full-color 3D printing, and AI converge, who is defining the future of 3D printing?  

(Hard Innovation Alliance is organized by Leiphone.)

Flashforge, Wande Mei, Xianyi... justo a ambos lados del stand de Atomic Reshape, impresoras 3D multicolor debutaban en grupo, y varias incluso exhibían sus propias impresoras 3D a todo color.

Yet, what matters more than the "price hike" itself is the signal it sends: after years of price wars, cloud providers are for the first time systematically passing cost pressures onto the market. That same afternoon, Baidu Intelligent Cloud quickly followed suit; earlier, AWS, Google Cloud, UCloud, and Tencent Cloud had already raised their prices one after another. Thus, an AI-driven "wave of computing power price increases" has now formed a global resonance. "If we don’t raise prices, costs really can’t hold up anymore," an industry insider long tracking the cloud sector told Leifeng.com. Over the past year, the explosion of AI applications has pushed demand for computing power to unprecedented heights; meanwhile, supply—including GPU capacity, data centers, and electricity—has struggled to expand at the same pace. When demand grows exponentially while supply remains constrained by physical limits, price becomes an inevitable variable. However, it is worth noting that this is not a "uniform" price increase. Facing similar cost pressures, different domestic cloud providers are making distinctly different choices: some are adjusting only AI-related services while leaving core offerings untouched, others are raising prices across the board, and still others are holding steady, attempting to seize market share through price differentiation. "If we don’t raise prices, everyone’s costs will become unsustainable." "Everyone in the industry knew this wave of price hikes was bound to come sooner or later," cloud sales representative Zhang Xiangyu told Leifeng.com bluntly. In his view, this is not an active choice by cloud providers but more of a passive adjustment. Changes on the demand side are the most direct driver.

excerpt_i18n.en:
At the start of this year, global software stock investors collectively experienced a "terrifying sixty days." From the end of last year to the beginning of this year, the market was still immersed in the illusion of an "AI application explosion." However, at the end of January, Anthropic unveiled Claude Cowork, capable of autonomously operating computers and handling office tasks, which directly shattered the valuation logic of traditional SaaS. In just two months, North American software stocks lost over $1.6 trillion in market value. A nearly desperate sentiment pervaded the market: if AI can already operate computers and take over business workflows like humans, have the graphical interfaces and business software painstakingly built over the past two decades become outdated productivity tools? Addressing these life-or-death questions, in an online roundtable hosted by Leiphone GAIR Live, three industry veterans with deep expertise in SaaS and complementary perspectives—He Run: Co-founder and CEO of Zhi Qu Bai Chuan; Daniel: Senior investor and business head at a major internet company; Wu Hao: Author of "SaaS Entrepreneurship Roadmap," angel investor in leading SaaS companies, and former executive president—engaged in a rigorous 90-minute dialogue, offering penetrating insights into the current state and future of SaaS.  
1. Recent Plunge in SaaS Stock Prices: Not Due to Financial Revenue, but Expectations Being Dimensionality-Reduced  
In Daniel's view, the sharp decline in SaaS is not due to SaaS companies' financial data falling short of expectations, but rather expectations being subjected to a dimensionality-reduction strike.
excerpt_i18n.es: A principios de este año, los inversores en acciones de software a nivel global experimentaron juntos una "aterradora sesenta días". Desde finales del año pasado hasta principios de este, el mercado aún estaba inmerso en la ilusión de la "gran explosión de aplicaciones de IA". Sin embargo, a finales de enero, Anthropic lanzó Claude Cowork, capaz de operar computadoras de forma autónoma y realizar tareas de oficina independientemente, lo que directamente destrozó la lógica de valoración del SaaS tradicional. En solo dos meses, las acciones de software en Norteamérica perdieron más de 1.6 billones de dólares en valor de mercado. El mercado se impregnó de un discurso casi desesperado: si la IA ya puede operar computadoras como un humano y hacerse cargo de los flujos de negocio, entonces, ¿qué sentido tienen las interfaces gráficas y los procesos comerciales que hemos construido con esfuerzo durante las últimas dos décadas?

items.raw_excerpt: We introduce exclusive self attention (XSA), a simple modification of self attention (SA) that improves Transformer’s sequence modeling performance. The key idea is to constrain attention to capture only information orthogonal to the token’s own value vector (thus excluding information of self position), encouraging better context modeling. Evaluated on the standard language modeling task, XSA consistently outperforms SA across model sizes up to 2.7B parameters and shows increasingly larger gains as sequence length grows.
